title: Extract coupling coefficients from gap SPP modes
action: For the binary metal-dielectric multilayer with layer thicknesses Au = 8.4 nm, MgF2 = 50 nm, Si = 200 nm at free-space wavelength 1550 nm, obtain the permittivities of Au, MgF2, and Si from standard references (e.g., Johnson‑Christy for Au, literature for MgF2 and Si) or a Drude model. Use eigenmode analysis to compute the propagation constants of symmetric and antisymmetric gap SPP modes for the metal‑dielectric‑metal gap and for coupling through the dielectric spacer, then calculate the coupling coefficients C+ (dielectric‑mediated) and C- (metal‑mediated) and the asymmetry constant η = C−/C+.
description: Required intermediate to obtain the coupling coefficients that determine the band dispersion.
output_schema: JSON object with fields: C_plus (float), C_minus (float), eta (float).

title: Band dispersion calculation for the binary metamaterial
action: Using the coupling coefficients C+ and C- from the previous step (or directly via the transfer matrix method for the same multilayer stack), compute the TM-polarized dispersion relation for the infinite binary metamaterial. Output propagation constants β as a function of the Bloch wave number κ ∈ [0, π] with at least 50 points.
description: Confirms the Dirac point at κ=0 and band inversion. The verifier compares the dispersion curves against hidden reference values derived from the paper.
output_schema: CSV with columns: kappa (float, dimensionless, range [0,π] with at least 50 points), beta_upper (float, normalized dimensionless propagation constant of the upper band), beta_lower (float, normalized dimensionless propagation constant of the lower band).

title: Surface mode existence map computation
action: For each pair (η, Z) with η ∈ [−2.0, −0.5] in steps of 0.1 and Z ∈ [−2.0, 2.0] in steps of 0.1, compute the two possible values of the decay parameter r from the analytic solution (the ‘+’ and ‘−’ branches) of the coupled-mode equations. A localized surface mode exists if at least one solution satisfies |r| < 1. Output the existence flag and the minimum |r| among the valid solutions (or the maximum |r| if no solution satisfies |r| < 1).
description: Maps the existence regions of surface modes in the η–Z plane. The verifier recomputes the existence flags from the analytic formula and compares.
output_schema: CSV with columns: eta (float), Z (float), exists (int 0/1), r_magnitude (float).
